newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares ends up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares ends up but off highs.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended up but off earlier highs on Monday as some investors took profits in the late afternoon session, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 7.76 points, or 1.20 percent, to close at 653.96 points after touching a high of 654.13 points in morning session.
Gainers led losers by 76 to 41, with 52 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue upwards on Tuesday as more investors re-entered the market after the New Year holiday combined with positive news from the domestic economy.
Brokers said they expected the market would give a full reaction to the state budget and other economic figures which were announced by President Suharto in parliament on Monday.
"Certain sectors including infrastructure will continue to enjoy positive sentiment after the announcement of the state budget," a broker with a Japanese firm said.
Brokers said strong regional markets combined with fresh buying of certain heavyweights in the morning session to boost overall market sentiment in Jakarta.
Brokers said some investors were likely to continue buying actively in certain counters as they had re-evaluated their portfolios for the new year.
"As usual, some of them are switching or adding to their portfolios early in the year," a local broker said.
Telecommunications firm Telkom, toll operator Citra Marga, cement producer Indocement, timber firm Barito Pacific and Bank Negara Indonesia were among the gainers on fresh buying, brokers said.
Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 4,275 rupiah on 5.9 million shares after touched a high of 4,375 rupiah earlier.
